speaker: n
text: In this town, every person is born with a clock on their wrist.

speaker: n
text: It shows exactly when they're going to die.

speaker: n
text: Most people get seventy years. Eighty, if they're lucky.

speaker: n
text: My name is Leo, and this morning, my clock said one day left.

speaker: n
text: I'm twelve. I'm not even sick. My mom saw it and started crying.

speaker: mom
text: Leo, the clocks are never wrong.

speaker: n
text: I ran to school to tell my best friend, Mia. She grabbed my arm.

speaker: mia
text: Leo, look at everyone else's clocks.

speaker: n
text: The baker had two days left. The mailman had three. Every kid in my class had less than a week.

speaker: n
text: Then I noticed something strange. Every time the old clock tower rang, everyone's clock jumped down.

speaker: n
text: Everyone except one man. The mayor. His clock said nine hundred years.

speaker: n
text: That night, Mia and I snuck into the clock tower.

speaker: n
text: Inside, thousands of glowing hourglasses floated in the air. One for every person in town. Each one had a name on it. Mine was almost empty.

speaker: n
text: A thin golden stream was pouring out of every hourglass, straight into a giant clock in the middle of the room.

speaker: n
text: Suddenly, the doors slammed shut. The mayor stepped out of the shadows.

speaker: mayor
text: You shouldn't be here, Leo. Your time is up.

speaker: n
text: My clock started beeping. Ten seconds. Nine. Eight.

speaker: mia
text: Leo, the gears! Stop the gears!

speaker: n
text: I spotted a huge lever beside the giant clock. Three seconds. I jumped and pulled it with everything I had.

speaker: n
text: The gears screeched to a stop. Every hourglass flipped upside down. The golden time poured out of the tower, back into every house in town.

speaker: n
text: My clock jumped. One day. Ten years. Seventy-five years.

speaker: n
text: The mayor screamed. His clock spun backwards, faster and faster, until it cracked, and he crumbled into sand.

speaker: n
text: The next morning, the whole town was outside, laughing and comparing clocks. Everyone had their years back.

speaker: n
text: I thought it was over. Until I looked at Mia's wrist. Her clock was blank. No numbers. Nothing.

speaker: n
text: She just smiled at me and whispered,

speaker: mia
text: Leo, I was never born in this town.
